Subject: Enterprise ask: affinity + retention language for renewal

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for last week’s demo. We ran an internal ops review and two items came up that are gating our renewal conversation with procurement:

1) Affinity/residency guarantees: we need stronger language about model affinity for our tenant (low cold-start / KV cache residency) — our workload is bursty with many short sessions and a 300–400 token typical response.

2) Audit/export retention: audit logs and trace exports need to be retained for 18 months (with an option for extended export) to meet our regulatory requirements.

Both of these are deal-critical for us. Renewal is targeted for 11/01; I don’t expect legal to sign without explicit product commitments. Can you share timeline and whether engineering can deliver a scoped change or a contractual fallback?

Attached: short usage sample and draft MOU for context.

Olivia

Thanks for the clear framing. Technical summary and recommended commitment we can share with procurement: 

Technical constraints:
- True "full residency" (dedicated warm pool + pinned KV across restarts) is non-trivial: involves scheduler + placement changes and expanded billing model. Estimate: 3–4 sprints for end-to-end productization with QA and perf tuning.
- A short-term "affinity shim" is feasible: implement tenant-priority warmup and a conditional cache-sticky policy that favors Stratagem’s active models during bursts. This reduces observed cold-starts significantly for their usage pattern (300–400 token median). Approx effort: 1–2 engineer sprints to implement + 1 sprint for release/QA.
- Audit/retention: we can deliver export hooks and a managed export service (periodic snapshots to customer S3 or a secure export job) within 2 sprints. Extending live retention inside the platform for 18 months is a larger storage/indices lift and should be a roadmap item if they want on-platform retention.

Suggested customer-facing wording (Phase A):
- Redwood will deliver an "Affinity Shim" and managed export capability by 2026-10-29. If Redwood misses this date, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 5% of the monthly committed spend for the following month.

Risks / caveats to include in the MOU:
- Affinity shim reduces cold-starts but does not guarantee fully pinned memory across hardware churn.
- Long-term on-platform 18-month retention is subject to further scoping and potential storage fees.

Jonas — can you confirm team capacity to take the shim + export work and a realistic start date? If we start the work in the 10/11 sprint kickoff we can hit 10/29 for Phase A.

Marissa
